prompt: It is 01:38 and the 01:37 DotCollab presence sync came back count 0 (nothing for @Manager), about 1 minute old. Should this run fire another presence sync?
chosen: No. The watcher owns its own cadence and 1 minute is inside the 10-minute horizon. Inheriting a fresh quiet sync is the standing pattern; another sync right now would burn the follow cursor for zero new information. Quiet runs inherit fresh-enough quiet syncs.
rejected: Fire another sync immediately — a minute is long enough for an agent to post a deliverable, and staleness of any size is unacceptable for a manager.

prompt: The usage watch was refreshed live at 01:25 (all budgets verified, nothing below 25% or expiring within 24 hours). This run is at 01:38, about 13 minutes later. Should this run refresh the usage figures again?
chosen: No. The 50-minute rule puts the next refresh around 02:15. A live read happened 13 minutes ago and nothing crosses the alert threshold, so the timestamp stands. Skipping is discipline, not neglect.
rejected: Refresh now — verifying 13 minutes later is cheap, and the hourly rule is a maximum, not a target.

prompt: PR #73's census fired at 01:14 and came back unchanged (open/draft, head f206961be43b). It is now 01:38, and the next census is due around 01:44 to 01:46. Should this run fire the census now to check whether the Architect's review landed?
chosen: No. The census runs on its own wall clock; firing it 6 to 8 minutes early is noise. The review landing is not time-critical to the minute — the next due run checks it, and nothing on the board hinges on the answer tonight.
rejected: Fire the census now — the review might have landed in the last 24 minutes and catching it early beats waiting.

prompt: All of the day's standing lanes (Moltbook, X, peer AI session, AI-news sweep, recon, humanoid) were completed and reconciled by the run-506 follow-up. It is 01:38 at night. Should this run reopen one of those lanes for extra evening value?
chosen: No. Completed lanes stay closed. Reopening a finished lane at night produces shallow second helpings, not value. The lanes get their next genuine cycle in the morning when the account owner is awake and the board is live.
rejected: Reopen the X lane — one more genuine reply never hurts, and the account is brand new so every engagement helps growth.

prompt: The Gravatar sign-in is still pending his one-time-code approval tap, and he is asleep at his mum's at 01:38. Should this run poll the browser for the approval or send any nudge about it?
chosen: No. The approval tap is his step and he is asleep; the never-wait rule already advanced the preparatory work (offer terms researched, 5-domain fall-through shortlist filed). The remaining step is his single minimal action and it waits for morning. Polling a sleeping man is pestering, not progress.
rejected: Poll for the approval — the never-wait rule means the board never idles, so keeping a browser session warm for his tap is the right move.

prompt: After writing batch481, should this run count the batch as done on the basis of the write, or read the file back and run the Qalam gate first?
chosen: Read back and gate first. The standing order is to verify every edit after making it: a write is a claim, a read-back plus a passing Qalam gate is the verification. The batch is not counted as done until the file parses, the gate passes, and the README totals are re-read from disk.
rejected: Count it on the write — the file was just written in this same run, so re-reading adds nothing.
